groups.label: Moral Inquiries and Justice
groups.summary: These entries trace the initial inquiry into justice, from Cephalus and Polemarchus's traditional maxims through Glaucon and Adeimantus's demands to see justice valued for its own sake rather than external rewards. They also analyze the overarching structure of the dialogue, the developmental progression of interlocutors, and the shifting role of Socrates from questioning critic to constructive guide.
groups.rationale: All children address the foundational dialectic of Books I-II regarding the definition and inherent value of justice, alongside the structural evolution of the characters and arguments framing that inquiry.

groups.label: Civic Order and Education
groups.summary: Focusing on Books II and III, these entries examine the emergence of the guardian class from the luxurious state and the strict educational regimen designed to form them. They detail reforms including the purification of theology, prohibitions on dramatic imitation, simplifications of musical modes and physical gymnastics, and the legitimizing myth of the metals.
groups.rationale: These entries form a continuous, cohesive sequence outlining the social origin, cultural censorship, physical and musical training, and mythic caste structure of the guardian class.

groups.label: Cosmology and Historical Models
groups.summary: This group explores theoretical, cosmological, and institutional frameworks across the dialogue, from the political allegory of the cave's dual eyesight disorders to the mathematical cycle of the Platonic number. It also evaluates the Republic's dual Spartan and ideal nature, the mythic astronomical model of Er, and the historical precedents offered by the Pythagorean League.
groups.rationale: These commentary passages cover the advanced philosophical allegories, mathematical and cosmological structures, and external historical-political archetypes (Pythagorean and Spartan) shaping the dialogue.
